transcript.text: washing machine making a horrible noise
From what you have described, the most likely cause is load size / distribution (imbalance). Next: Try an ordinary evenly-distributed load to rule out load imbalance. Let me know what you find.
It's not the load, it's every spin now. Gets louder the faster it spins, like a jet engine. Washes and drains fine though.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is drum bearings. Check how the drum moves by hand. With the machine unplugged and the door open, how does the drum feel when you turn it by hand — normal, much lighter or looser than usual, or stiff, rough or grinding?
It rumbles and grinds when I turn it by hand.

With the machine unplugged and the door open, push the drum firmly down and lift it up, then rock it side to side. Does the drum feel loose — dropping, knocking or clunking — or firm with just a slight springy movement?
Yes, there's a noticeable clunky up-and-down play when I lift the edge of the drum.

[Heading: Likely cause: drum bearing]
The checks point to the drum bearing. To find the right part, could you give me the make and model number? It is usually on a sticker inside the door rim or on the back of the door.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Zanussi, model ZWF81443W. It's about 9 years old, is it worth fixing?

[Heading: Likely cause: drum bearing]
It depends on whether the bearings on your model can be replaced on their own or need a whole new drum and tub, and how that cost compares with a new machine. On a 9-year-old washer that washes and drains fine, it can be worth it if the bearing part is available, but a quote from a parts supplier or engineer will settle it. The checks point to the drum bearing. I could not find a confirmed match for model ZWF81443W in our parts catalogue, so check with the manufacturer or a parts supplier using the full model number, or ask an appliance engineer to fit it.
